Set point actually does make sense, but not in the way that fats want it to. It has to do with unconscious self-regulation and an "understanding" of how much calories you eat. "Naturally" thin people have a tendency to overestimate how many calories they eat, and to self-regulate to a lower number of calories. "Naturally" fat people have a tendency to underestimate how many calories they eat, and to self-regulate to a higher number of calories. If both of those groups of people were allowed to eat food in whatever quantities they desired, the non-hams would eat less than the hams without having to put much thought into it. This is why "dieting doesn't work" -- because if you have a tendency to underestimate the amount of food you're eating, you will regain weight. And if you eat a certain amount of calories every day without thinking about it, you'll maintain a certain weight without thinking about it.
